provenance.note: ffmpeg and ffprobe are vendored as separate, pre-built executables fetched by scripts/fetch-ffmpeg.mjs into a gitignored vendor/ directory at build time — never committed, never `pnpm add`-ed, never linked against Loombre's own code. Every platform pinned below ships a GPL build (GPL-2.0-or-later or GPL-3.0-or-later depending on source — see each platform's `license` field) because Loombre needs libx264/libx265 for H.264/HEVC transcoding, which FFmpeg's default LGPL configuration cannot provide.
provenance.aggregationRationale: Loombre's server/worker (AGPL-3.0 relicense target, see /LICENSE-INTENT.md) invoke ffmpeg/ffprobe strictly as separate child processes (packages/jobs job workers spawn them, communicate over argv + stdio/pipes + exit codes) — never dlopen'd, never statically or dynamically linked into a Loombre binary, never sharing an address space or a build. This is the FSF's own 'mere aggregation' case (GPL FAQ: 'if the programs communicate through pipes ... that is a fairly strong indicator that they are separate programs'), reinforced here by process-isolation: the installer tarball ships them as distinct executables in bin/ and vendor/ffmpeg/, not part of the linked `dist/` output. AGPL-3.0 does not forbid an AGPL work distributed on the same medium as unrelated GPL executables; each retains its own license and neither is a derivative of the other.

provenance.verificationPosture: Every entry's sha256 was checked in one of two ways, recorded per-entry in `verification.method`: (a) 'independently downloaded and hashed' — this lane fetched the actual bytes and computed sha256 itself; or (b) 'publisher-checksums-file' — taken from the upstream project's own signed/published checksums file without a redundant full download here (still real bytes-in-hand where noted). Any MISMATCH found against a publisher's own webpage-published checksum is called out explicitly in that entry's `verification.notes` — see macos-arm64.

macos-x64.licenseNote: evermeet.cx (Landon Fuller) publishes its exact `ffmpeg` build configure invocation on-page: includes --enable-gpl --enable-version3 --enable-libx264 --enable-libx265 — --enable-version3 is FFmpeg's own flag for 'this build is GPLv3, not GPLv2', so GPL-3.0-or-later is a direct read of the publisher's stated configuration, not an inference. evermeet.cx explicitly does NOT build for Apple Silicon (see 'apple-silicon-arm' page linked from their FAQ: 'I do not plan to provide native ffmpeg binaries for Apple Silicon ARM') — this entry is Intel/x86_64 only; it runs under Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon Macs but macos-arm64 below is the native-arm pin.

verification.notes: Downloaded both zips in full and sha256'd locally; each contains exactly one flat file (`ffmpeg` / `ffprobe`, no wrapper directory) whose size matches evermeet's own JSON release-info API (evermeet.cx/ffmpeg/info/ffmpeg/release) exactly. evermeet publishes a detached GPG .sig per file instead of a plain sha256 on-page — this pin's sha256 is this lane's own hash of the bytes it downloaded, not transcribed from the publisher, so it is exact for THIS pin but a future re-pin must re-download+re-hash (fetch-ffmpeg.mjs's own checksum-verify step, not a comparison against a publisher-listed value).

macos-arm64.licenseNote: osxexperts.net publishes its build script on-page: ./configure --enable-gpl --enable-libx264 --enable-libx265 ... with NO --enable-version3 flag present anywhere in the visible script. FFmpeg's own convention is --enable-gpl alone = GPLv2-or-later; --enable-version3 is required to opt into GPLv3. No LICENSE.txt ships in the zip (just the bare binary) to cross-check against, so this is read directly from the publisher's own build script, not confirmed via bundled license text the way linux-x64/macos-x64 are — flagged for lane I4 to re-verify (e.g. by asking `ffmpeg -L`/-version banner text, which FFmpeg embeds at build time) before this pin ships.
